verifications.claim: SpaceX successfully launched 25 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Monday, April 6, 2026, at 4:03 p.m. PT.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "successfully launched 25 Starlink satellites from its Falcon 9 rocket... Vandenberg Space Force Base... April 6, 2026"; "Starlink Mission Falcon 9 SLC-4E, California... April 6, 2026"; "Monday, April 6: Starlink 17-35... 25 Starlink satellites... Falcon 9... Vandenberg... Launch window: 4:03 to 8:03 p.m. PT"; "Monday SpaceX launch today carried 25 Starlink satellites... Vandenberg... April 6, opening at 4:03 p.m. PT"; R1 also "scheduled for Monday at 7:49 p.m. PT"
verifications.reasoning: All major details (success, 25 satellites, Falcon 9, location, date) directly supported across sources; exact liftoff time of 4:03 p.m. described as window opening, not confirmed precise liftoff (one source notes 7:49 p.m. target within window).

verifications.claim: The launch followed a Sunday scrub.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The launch was originally scheduled for Sunday evening"; "Sunday Scrub Pushed The First Mission To Monday... scrubbed today due to upper-level wind shears"
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by explicit mentions of Sunday scrub/delay in both sources.

verifications.claim: The mission launched from Space Launch Complex 4E.

verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as SLC-4E across all sources.

verifications.claim: SpaceX has additional Starlink missions scheduled for April 8, 9, and 11, 2026, according to the official SpaceX launch schedule.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2 (official SpaceX): Starlink SLC-4E April 10, Starlink SLC-40 April 14, NG-24 SLC-40 April 11 (not Starlink), no April 8/9 Starlink; R3/R4: Starlink April 9 SLC-4E
verifications.reasoning: Official SpaceX schedule (R2) lacks Starlink missions on April 8, 9, 11 (April 11 is non-Starlink); other sources list April 9 Starlink, creating contradiction on specific dates.

verifications.reasoning: Directly described as two-stage rocket in context of Starlink missions.
